RagShortTexts: Seville commands the Guadalquivir inland port, distinguished by the soaring Giralda tower.

Variants.Content: Recaptured in 1248, Seville serves as the royal capital of Lower Andalusia. Situated where the tidal Guadalquivir remains navigable for ocean galleys, ships dock beneath the twelve-sided Torre del Oro. Its Great Mosque minaret became the Giralda bell tower, overlooking the Reales Alcázares where Mudéjar plasterwork adorns Christian halls.

Tens of thousands of fertile olive groves were redistributed to Christian repopulators. Seville provides the military base for campaigns pressing toward Granada, regulating maritime fleets and river trade.
The river bustles with lateen-rigged barges loading olive oil and sweet Andalusian wines. Even in uncertain times, working the wharves pays honest copper to keep bread on family tables.
